6; / \
7; | '87 T2 Turbonator LM codebase |
8; | Mopar ECM |
9; | 1987 Turbo II |
10; | |
11; | Code and original design and data Copyright � 1985 by Chrysler Corporation |
12; | |
13; | Other code modules are Copyright 2010 by Robert Lloyd |
14; | |
15; | |
16; | 1) Replaced TRANSM with CONFIG - a full cal option flag constant similar |
17; | to the CONFIG constant + OPTION flags used on the '89 T1. Changed all |
18; | of the auto trans checks to look for the 'new' auto config flag. All |
19; | of the new and previous cal options are configurable by config flags. |
20; | This allows features to be added to the cal without the need to |
21; | re-assemble the code. |
22; | |
23; | 2) Added switchable boost. Similar in operation to the later code, but the |
24; | low setting is set by a single constant rather than a boost x rpm |
25; | table (similar to the S60 implementation). |
26; | |
27; | 3) Added alky injection control routine (with help from Brian Bucar on the |
28; | function of the system). The alky injection can control the pump and up |
29; | to 2 separate alky injectors, triggered by MAP constants. This uses the |
30; | Cruise, and EGR/Purge solenoids. So, cannot be used with those at the |
31; | same time. Also cannot be used with the Speed Sensitive Aero option at |
32; | at the same time. The code checks if both options are enabled, if they |
33; | are, then neither will run. |
34; | |
35; | 4) Added Anti-lag Retard routine. This routine looks at the delta to boost |
36; | goal and pulls up to 16 deg based on this delta (could be configured |
37; | for 32 degrees as well). It will only pull timing at WOT (and so should |
38; | no affect emmisions or driveability) except when the staging limiter is |
39; | active to help spoolup off the line for manual cars. There were some |
40; | code changes to the staging limiter code to support this function. But |
41; | the functionality of the staging limiter is the same as previous. |
42; | |
43; | 5) Staging Limiter Changes. Re-coded for simplicity. Added the option to |
44; | enable the staging limiter by switch. Default is setup for the brake |
45; | switch (useful for ATX cars). |
46; | |
47; | 6) Added WOT Battery volts target. This can be used to either increase or |
48; | decrease (or turn off) the alternator output when at WOT. |
49; | |
50; \___________________________________________________________________________/

65; Version 12
66; 10/12/10 - Complete re-write of the code starting with a fresh dis-assembled
67; source. Converted naming conventions to be common with T-SMEC and
68; T_SBEC whereever possible for variables, table data and
69; subroutines.
70; - Added Battery Volts Target for WOT operation. Allows you to set a
71; different bat volts at WOT to either disable the alternator
72; (by setting the value low) or to increase the output (by setting
73; it high).
74; - Added several stock 2.2 templates including the SL 2.2 Auto cal.
75;
76; Version 12.1
77; 02/01/11 - Fixed the definitions for STRNTR_SparkStartRunTransferPointRpm and
78; RNSTTR_SparkRunStartTransferPointRpm that was causing a starting
79; issue.
80;
81; Version 12.2
82; 02/08/11 - Added the CEFlash routine call from the main loop (omitted by mis-
83; take.
84;
85; Version 12.3
86; 02/10/11 - Removed the WOT Battery volts target code that was causing a
87; no-start condition.
88;
89; Version 12.4
90; 02/23/11 - Changed the STRNTR and RNSTTR values back to 16-bit constant
91; lookups like v10 (and the same as T-SMEC).
92; - Changed the scale of the speed cutoof in the staging limiter from
93; 0-127mph to 0-255mph.
94; - Fixed the RPM references for many constant/table values.
95; - Fixed the Error Bit reference after the checksum routine.
96; - Removed the Alky code for now. Need to find more processor time to
97; re-enable it.
98;
99; Version 12.5
100; 04/27/11 - Fixed the definition for the RTMAPE. Was not being scaled with MAP
101; correctly. Template change only.
102;
103; Version 13.0
104; 06/06/11 - Updated .asm and template files to be MP Tuner 2 compatible.
105;

114;
115; Bit functions: (derived from Ladybug development)
116; Many bytes in the RAM contain status bits. For each of these the address value
117; was separated into bit numbers, for example BitFlags_7f has b7f_bit7 through b7f_bit0.
118; As the function of the bits is decoded, a global replace is performed to replace
119; the bit name with a meaningful name, like:
120;
121; b7f_SparkEngineNotRunning = $%10000000 ; -10000000-
122; ^ NOTE: no leading 0x
123;
124; When working with bits, you can add several together using the "or" operator | like this:
125;
126; [b50_SparkEngineNotRunning | b50_BaroSolEnergized] ; -10100000-
127; ^ NOTE: Square brackets, not round ^
128;
129; The inverse function ~ sets all bits except the ones specified, so:
130;
131; ~b50_SparkEngineNotRunning ; -01111111-
132;
133; You can combine the inverse ~ with the or | like this:
134;
135; ~[b50_SparkEngineNotRunning | b50_BaroSolEnergized] ; -01011111-
136;
137; The intent here is to make the logical functionality of the code easier to follow.
138;
139; ***********************************************************************
140; Calibration Template definition
141; *****************************************************************************
142;
143; This template format will be used from T-LM v10 and later.
144;
145; I decided to switch to this format because it was getting clumsy
146; trying to define the switches for all of the build options (MTX/ATX,
147; 2.2/2.5, boost control, etc.). This way, all the calibration data can be
148; kept together in 1 place.
149;
150; Filename format:
151;
152; T-LM_[displ]_[trans]_[ID]_[version].asm
153;
154; For example, the 1st tempalte file I made was from the 89 T1 Auto:
155;
156; T-LM_22_MTX_a171_T2.asm
157;
158; This way you can start your T-SMEC build with any calibration. Though,
159; you may have to build a template file if you want a calibration that
160; does not already have a template file.
161;
162;
163;
164; !!! This line is now written by MP Tuner when you specify the template to build with. !!!

6434 ; new staging mod, RCL
6435 ; this simply decides which rev limit to use for 'normal' operation

6437 ; it uses the original code to turn off the fuel...

6445 ; here, check that the brake pedal is pushed (RCL)

6448 anda Z83_PortCdata ; comapre the switch state to the enable switch - if 2 switches are enabled, then they work as -OR- switches, not -AND-
6449 beq clearflag ; branch if not enabled or pedal just released
6450

6454 asld ;

7332UseCELForKnockIndication_MM:

7374; ********************
7375; pump control routine
7376; ********************
7377 
7378; AlkyPump_Control_MM:
7379;
7380; ldaa CONFIG_ConfigurationFlags
7381; bita #cfg_AlkyInj ; check the bit for Alky Injection
7382; beq AlkyPump_Return ; branch if the bit is not set, ie not enabled
7383; bita #cfg_ShiftLight ; check the bit for Speed Sensitive Aero
7384; bne AlkyPump_Return ; branch if the bit is set, can't run both of these routines
7385;
7386; ldaa MapValue
7387; ldab Z83_CPU_Port1_copy
7388; cmpa AKPMON_AlkyPumpOnSetpointFromMAP
7389; bcs AlkyPump_CheckHysteresisAndTurnOff ;if MAP is lower than the setpoint, see if it's lower than the 'off' point
7390; andb ~#CPU_Port1_PurgeEGR ;or whichever output you're going to use, this sets the bit to turn on the pump
7391; jmp AlkyPump_Return
7392;
7393; AlkyPump_CheckHysteresisAndTurnOff:
7394; cmpa AKPMOF_AlkyPumpOffSetpointFromMAP
7395; bcc AlkyPump_Return ; MAP is still higher than the 'off' setpoint
7396; orab #CPU_Port1_PurgeEGR ;turn off the pump
7397;
7398; AlkyPump_Return:
7399; stab Z83_CPU_Port1_copy
7400; rts
7401 
7402; ************************
7403; injector control routine
7404; ************************
7405; .msg "..." ; these are just messages to display during assemble to let you know what's going on...
7406 
7407; AlkyInjector_Control_MM:
7408;
7409; ; first, check to see if inj1 is already on, if it is, then check to see if it needs to be turned off, then maybe check inj2 turn on
7410; ldaa CONFIG_ConfigurationFlags
7411; bita #cfg_AlkyInj ; check the bit for Alky Injection
7412; beq AlkyInj_Return ; branch if the bit is not set, ie not enabled
7413; bita #cfg_ShiftLight ; check the bit for Speed Sensitive Aero
7414; bne AlkyInj_Return ; branch if the bit is set, can't run both of these routines
7415;
7416; ldab Z83_CPU_Port1_copy
7417; orab ~#CPU_Port1_CruiseVent ;clear all bits in AccB except for this one
7418; andb ~#CPU_Port1_CruiseVent
7419; bne AlkyInj1_CheckHysteresisAndTurnOff ;branch if the bit for inj1 is set
7420;
7421; ;inj1 is not already on, so check the MAP level
7422;
7423; ldaa MapValue
7424; cmpa AKI1ON_AlkyInj1OnSetpointFromMAP
7425; bcs AlkyInj1_CheckHysteresisAndTurnOff ;if MAP is lower than the setpoint, see if it's lower than the 'off' point
7426; andb ~#CPU_Port1_CruiseVent ;or whichever output you're going to use, this sets the bit to turn on inj 1
7427; jmp AlkyInj_Return
7428;
7429; AlkyInj1_CheckHysteresisAndTurnOff:
7430; cmpa AKI1OF_AlkyInj1OffSetpointFromMAP
7431; bcc AlkyInj_Return ; MAP is still higher than the 'off' setpoint
7432; orab #CPU_Port1_CruiseVent ;turn off inj 1
7433; stab Z83_CPU_Port1_copy
7434;
7435; AlkyInj_CheckInj2:
7436; ldaa MapValue
7437; cmpa AKI2ON_AlkyInj2OnSetpointFromMAP
7438; bcs AlkyInj2_CheckHysteresisAndTurnOff ;if MAP is lower than the setpoint, see if it's lower than the 'off' point
7439; andb ~#CPU_Port1_CruiseVac ;or whichever output you're going to use, this sets the bit to turn on inj 2
7440; jmp AlkyInj_Return
7441;
7442; AlkyInj2_CheckHysteresisAndTurnOff:
7443; cmpa AKI2OF_AlkyInj2OffSetpointFromMAP
7444; bcc AlkyInj_Return ; MAP is still higher than the 'off' setpoint
7445; orab #CPU_Port1_CruiseVac ;turn off inj 1
7446;
7447; AlkyInj_Return:
7448; stab Z83_CPU_Port1_copy
7449; rts

7451; ************************
7452; Anti-lag Retard Routine
7453; ************************
7454 
7455CalculateAntiLagRetard_Routine_MM:
7456 ldaa 0x00 ; load 0x00 into A, default anti-lag retard
7457; check that the option is enabled...
7458 ldab CONFIG_ConfigurationFlags
7459 bitb #cfg_AntiLag
7460 beq AntiLag_return ;return if not enabled ; anti-lag retard = 0
7461; check the conditions for anti-lag - 1st check for the staging limiter, then for WOT, then for negative MAP
7462 ldab BitFlags_7f
7463 bitb #b7f_bit5 ;using this bit to tell that the limiter is active - for the anti-lag retard
7464 bne L3000 ;branch if the bit is set; if set, ignore the WOT requirement, otherwise check for WOT
7465 ldab BitFlags_81
7466 lsrb ;bitb #b81_FullThrottle
7467 bcc AntiLag_return ; return if not WOT ; anti-lag retard = 0
7468L3000: ldab BoostTarget ; load the target boost
7469 subb MapValue ; subtract the actual MAP value
7470 bcs AntiLag_return ; branch if greater or equal - no need for antilag ; anti-lag retard = 0
7471 tba ; move DeltaMAP to A for the lookup
7472 ldx #ANTLAG_AntiLagRetardfromBoostTargetDelta ; load index with value
7473 jsr Lookup4ByteTable ; call:
7474 lsra ; divide result by 2
7475 lsra ; divide result by 2
7476 lsra ; divide result by 2 - total dived by 8
7477 
7478AntiLag_return:
7479 staa AntiLagRetard ; store the antilag retard
7480 rts

7486ControlShiftLight_Routine_MM:
7487 ldaa Counter_MainLoop1 ; load a with memory contents
7488 bita #0x20
7489 bne ShiftLight_return ; branch if not equal (not zero)
7490 ldab CONFIG_ConfigurationFlags
7491 bitb #cfg_ShiftLight
7492 beq ShiftLight_return ; return if not enabled
7493 ldaa BitFlags_82 ; load a with memory contents
7494 bmi ShiftLight_return ; branch if b82_EngineNotRunning set - Engine Not Running (hi bit 1)
7495 
7496ShiftLight_Run:
7497 ldab Z83_CPU_Port1_copy
7498 ldx EngineRpm_HB
7499 cpx SLRPM_ShiftLightSetpoint
7500 bcs ShiftLight_OFF ; if RPM is lower than the setpoint, clear bits to turn light off
7501ShiftLight_ON:
7502 orab #CPU_Port1_PurgeEGR ; turn on the light
7503 stab Z83_CPU_Port1_copy
7504 jmp ShiftLight_return
7505 
7506ShiftLight_OFF:
7507 andb ~#CPU_Port1_PurgeEGR ; turn off the light
7508 stab Z83_CPU_Port1_copy
7509 
7510ShiftLight_return:
7511 rts
